parts.text:
Experiment 1
3 3
Use the large measuring cylinder to pour 50cm of distilled water and 40cm of sulfuric acid
into the 250cm conical flask.
3 3
Use the small measuring cylinder to add 2cm of methyl orange and 5cm of solution J to the
mixture in the conical flask. Measure the temperature of the mixture and record it in the table.
Use the small measuring cylinder to now start the reaction by adding 5cm of solution K to the
conical flask and immediately start your timer and swirl the mixture.
Measure the time taken for the mixture to turn very pale yellow and record the time in the table.
Measure and record the final temperature of the mixture.
Experiment 2
Repeat Experiment 1 but heat the mixture in the conical flask to about 30°C before adding the
solution K. Measure and record the temperature of the mixture.
Now add 5cm of solution K to the conical flask and immediately start your timer and swirl the
mixture.
Measure the time taken for the mixture to turn very pale yellow and record the time in the table.
Measure and record the final temperature of the mixture.
Experiment 3
Repeat Experiment 1 but heat the mixture in the conical flask to about 40°C before adding
the solution K to the conical flask. Take the same measurements and record the values in the
table.
Experiment 4
Repeat Experiment 1 but heat the mixture in the conical flask to about 50°C before adding
the solution K to the conical flask. Take the same measurements and record the values in the
table.
Work out the average temperatures to complete the table.

text: You are going to investigate the rate of a reaction between two solutions, J and K, and sulfuric acid
at different temperatures.
Read all the instructions below carefully before starting the experiments.
Instructions
You are going to carry out four experiments.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe the appearance of solid L.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Add about 10cm of distilled water to solid L and shake the mixture for about one minute to
dissolve.
Divide the solution into four equal portions in four test-tubes and carry out the following tests.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
Add several drops of aqueous ammonia to the first portion of the solution.
Now add excess ammonia solution to the mixture and shake.
observation ______

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
Add excess aqueous sodium hydroxide to the second portion of the solution.
observation ______

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text:
Add about 1cm of dilute nitric acid to the third portion of the solution followed by aqueous
silver nitrate.
observation ______

parts.label: (iv)
parts.text:
Add about 1cm of dilute nitric acid to the fourth portion of the solution followed by aqueous
barium nitrate.
observation ______

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Identify solid L.

tests on solid M

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Use a spatula to divide solid M into two portions in two test-tubes.
Heat the first portion of the solid, gently.
Test the gas given off with damp red litmus paper.
observation ______

parts.label: (e)
parts.text:
Dissolve the second portion of the solid in about 6cm of water. Pour half of the solution into a
boiling tube.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
Add about 1cm of aqueous sodium hydroxide to the solution in the boiling tube and heat
the mixture gently. Test the gas given off.
observation ______

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
Add about 1cm of dilute nitric acid to the remaining solution in the test-tube followed by
aqueous silver nitrate.
observation ______

text: You are provided with two solids, L and M, which are both salts.
Carry out the following tests on the solids, recording all of your observations at each stage.
tests on solid L
The label on a bottle of orange drink stated ‘contains no artificial colours’. A scientist thought that
the orange colour in the drink was a mixture of two artificial colours:
• Sunset Yellow E110
• Allura Red E129
Plan an investigation to show that the orange colour in the drink did not contain these two artificial
colours.
You are provided with samples of E110, E129 and the orange colouring from the drink. You are also
provided with common laboratory apparatus.
You may draw a diagram to help answer the question.
[Total: 6]
